blocks.content: It is often useful to work with partitioned matrices wherein each element in a matrix is itself a matrix. There are several ways to partition a matrix. For example, we could write the matrix C above as $$ \mathbf{C}=\begin{pmatrix}3&1&2\\2&5&4\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3&\vdots&1&2\\\cdots&\cdots&\cdots&\cdots\\2&\vdots&5&4\\1&\vdots&1&2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{a}&\mathbf{b}\\\mathbf{d}&\mathbf{B}\end{pmatrix} $$ where $$ \mathbf{a}=\left(3\right),\quad\mathbf{b}=\left(1\quad2\right),\quad\mathbf{d}=\left(2\atop1\right),\quad\mathbf{B}=\left(5\quad4\atop1\quad2\right) $$

Alternatively, we could partition C into a single row vector whose elements are themselves column vectors, $$ \mathbf{C}=\left(\begin{array}{l l l l}{\mathbf{c}_{1}}&{\mathbf{c}_{2}}&{\mathbf{c}_{3}}\end{array}\right)\quad\text{where}\quad\mathbf{c}_{1}=\left(\begin{array}{l}{3}\\ {2}\\ {1}\end{array}\right),\quad\mathbf{c}_{2}=\left(\begin{array}{l}{1}\\ {5}\\ {1}\end{array}\right),\quad\mathbf{c}_{3}=\left(\begin{array}{l}{2}\\ {4}\\ {2}\end{array}\right) $$ or C could be written as a column vector whose elements are row vectors, $$ \mathbf{C}=\left(\begin{array}{l}{\mathbf{b_{1}}}\\ {\mathbf{b_{2}}}\\ {\mathbf{b_{3}}}\end{array}\right)\quad\mathrm{w h e r e}\quad\mathbf{b_{1}}=\left(\begin{array}{l l l}{3}&{1}&{2}\end{array}\right),\quad\mathbf{b_{2}}=\left(\begin{array}{l l l}{2}&{5}&{4}\end{array}\right),\quad\mathbf{b_{3}}=\left(\begin{array}{l l l}{1}&{1}&{2}\end{array}\right) $$
